title: Topological Fermi-polaron Polaritons with Electrically Invertible Topology
authors: Xin Xie, Chenxi Liu, Yuze Liu, Lingxiao Zhou, Chulwon Lee, Yuhan Zhang, Nathanial Lydick, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kai Sun, Hui Deng
abstract: Topological polaritons provide a route to engineer optical Chern bands, but realizing large gaps or efficient electrical tunability remains challenging because time-reversal-symmetry breaking in semiconductor polariton systems is typically limited by weak Zeeman splittings. Here, we demonstrate a topological Bose-Fermi mixture --- Fermi-polaron polaritons ---where large gaps and electrically invertible topology emerge from the interplay of Fermi-polaron many-body interactions, photonic symmetry, and strong light--matter coupling. Using a gate-controlled monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenide integrated with a symmetry-engineered photonic crystal, we create Fermi-polaron polaritons with topological band structures. The direct coupling between band topology and gate-tunable many-body interactions provides a mechanism for amplified time-reversal-symmetry breaking beyond bare Zeeman splitting and enables electrical inversion of topological gaps, Berry curvature, and Chern numbers. These results establish an electrically reconfigurable platform for interaction-driven topological states and programmable topological photonics.
summary: The research presents a novel platform using Fermi-polaron polaritons in gated $	ext{MoSe}_2$ coupled to a Photonic Crystal to create topological states. By leveraging gate-tunable many-body interactions, the system achieves large, electrically switchable topological gaps and can invert its Chern number, establishing a programmable platform for topological photonics.
main_problem: The challenge is engineering optical Chern bands in polariton systems with large gaps and efficient electrical tunability, which is limited by weak time-reversal-symmetry (TRS) breaking mechanisms.
main_result: The authors demonstrate a Fermi-polaron polariton platform that achieves electrically controllable topological gaps and can invert topological invariants like the Chern number by tuning the gate voltage.
method: The study combines experimental characterization using momentum-resolved magneto-optical reflection contrast (RC) spectroscopy with theoretical modeling using coupled Hamiltonian approaches and FDTD/RCWA simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a topological Bose-Fermi mixture—Fermi-polaron polaritons—formed by coupling excitons/polarons in a gate-controlled monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenide ($	ext{MoSe}_2$) to the photonic modes of a symmetry-engineered Photonic Crystal (PhC).
key_observables: Topological invariants (Chern numbers, Berry curvature), polariton energy gaps ($\Delta E_{LP}$), and the sign/magnitude of the magneto-optical response (RMCD).
important_parameters: Gate voltage ($V_G$) controlling doping (hole/electron), external magnetic field ($B$), and the strength of light-matter coupling.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the coupled Hamiltonian model and relies on fitting resonance parameters from experimental spectra.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device structure, the gate-voltage dependence of polariton dispersions showing gap openings, and visualizations of the resulting Berry curvature maps confirming topological character.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the physical platform and the limitations of previous work, then detailing the experimental/theoretical methodology (RC/Hamiltonian modeling), presenting the key results showing gap opening and topological control, and concluding with the implications for programmable photonics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering of topological phases in coupled light-matter systems, providing a mechanism (interaction-driven TRS breaking) to achieve robust, electrically tunable topological properties in solid-state photonics, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and condensed matter theory.
